active_paradigms.description: Replace the exponential weighted moving average with Savitzky-Golay filter which fits local polynomials to smooth signals while preserving important features like peaks and slopes. The filter uses a window size matching the input (20 samples) with polynomial order 2-3 to smooth noise without distorting signal dynamics. This directly reduces slope change penalty (S) and false reversals (R) by providing smoother output while maintaining lower lag than simple moving averages. The filter is causal-aware through appropriate polyorder selection and works well across all signal types (sinusoidal, step changes, random walk).
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Slope changes (S), false reversals (R), and tracking accuracy while maintaining low lag
active_paradigms.cautions: Ensure polyorder < window_size, handle edge cases with 'extend' parameter, avoid over-smoothing by tuning polyorder (2-3 recommended)

active_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.signal.medfilt for robust noise-resistant filtering
active_paradigms.description: Implement median filtering which is robust to outliers and impulse noise that cause false slope reversals. Median filter preserves edges and step changes better than mean-based filters, directly addressing the step change test signal. Use odd kernel size (19 or 21) close to window_size for consistent processing. Median filtering reduces false reversals (R) and slope changes (S) by rejecting noise spikes that cause spurious directional changes. This is especially effective for non-stationary signals with random walk components.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: False reversals (R) and slope changes (S) for noisy non-stationary signals
active_paradigms.cautions: Kernel size must be odd, may introduce slight lag, combine with light smoothing if needed for very noisy signals

active_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.signal.wiener for adaptive statistical filtering
active_paradigms.description: Apply Wiener filter which estimates local statistics (mean and variance) within each window and adaptively smooths based on signal-to-noise ratio. Wiener filter automatically adjusts smoothing strength per window - strong smoothing in high-variance regions, minimal smoothing in low-variance regions. This directly minimizes lag error (L_recent and L_avg) by adapting to local signal characteristics while reducing noise-induced slope changes. Works well across all signal types including sinusoidal, step changes, and random walks.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Lag error (L_recent, L_avg) and adaptive noise reduction across varying signal characteristics
active_paradigms.cautions: MySize parameter should match window_size (20), ensure signal length >= mySize, may need post-processing for very short signals
